result.title: How Latent Transition Geometry Matters for Planning in World Models
result.summary: World models support planning by predicting how the environment evolves under candidate actions. However, one-step predictive accuracy alone does not characterize multi-step planning utility, which depends on distinguishing candidate futures. This raises a natural question: How does latent transition geometry shape planning? We investigate this through an action-conditioned transition-field view, using curvature regularization as a controlled intervention. Across four continuous-control tasks, appropriately tuned regularization improves planning, while excessive regularization can be detrimental. By decomposing the transition field into affine and non-affine components, we find that regularization reduces action sensitivity mainly through the non-affine component. To assess its role in planning, we directly manipulate the non-affine action response in frozen models and show that it affects candidate selection and closed-loop success. Further analysis shows that curvature generally brings predicted futures closer together, while preserving more of the differences along the goal direction. This helps explain why the planning effects vary across tasks. We observe broadly consistent planning trends across five sampling- and gradient-based solvers on LeWM and similar rollout-geometry trends on DINO-WM. Qualitative attention visualizations reveal accompanying shifts toward task-relevant visual structure. Together, these findings clarify how latent transition geometry influences multi-step planning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从动作条件转移场视角研究世界模型的潜在转移几何如何影响多步规划：以曲率正则化作为受控干预，在四个连续控制任务上检验其影响，并把转移场分解为仿射与非仿射成分，定位动作敏感性下降的来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把多步规划效用与单步预测精度分离，并在冻结模型中直接操纵非仿射响应做干预的思路，可供核查 LVR 中潜在状态几何是否真正支撑多步候选比较与最终答案使用，属可借鉴的诊断手段。
